warnings: The previous blocking issues are resolved: the train/test split is now subject-level rather than sample-level, and contrastive_loss() no longer performs an invalid reduction that would raise a runtime error.
The implemented LOSO split is hard-coded to five synthetic subjects with the fifth subject always held out. This is a demonstration rather than a general LOSO implementation.

Temporal mean pooling before contrastive learning is a modeling choice that discards temporal information. Whether this is appropriate depends on the intended architecture and is not inherently incorrect.
prepare_eeg_data() uses synthetic random data rather than real EEG data, so it is not suitable for evaluating research performance.
torch.manual_seed(42) inside prepare_eeg_data() makes every invocation generate the same dataset, which may be undesirable outside deterministic testing.
The shape check verifies equality but does not explicitly validate the expected tensor rank before reducing over dim=2.
suggested_fixes: Generalize the subject split to support an arbitrary number of subjects and arbitrary held-out subject indices.
Validate that the inputs are three-dimensional before applying mean(dim=2).
Separate deterministic test-data generation from production data-loading logic.
Document that temporal pooling is an intentional architectural choice if this implementation is used as an InfoNCE baseline.
final_review.summary: The diff resolves the previously identified blocking issues. The subject split is now subject-level, eliminating the prior train/test leakage, and contrastive_loss() implements a valid symmetric InfoNCE-style objective without the previous runtime error. No new blocking regressions were introduced.
